description: A sphere pooling open compute and knowledge so that powerful AI research is a public good, not a private moat. Members share GPUs, datasets and mentorship in the spirit of the gift.
name: AI Commons

value_cards.because: The most powerful AI systems will shape the century. If only a handful of companies control the compute, they control the future. That is not acceptable.
value_cards.care_about: Treating access to AI processing power the way we treat roads and water — something managed for collective benefit, not private advantage.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Open compute that serves open-washing — free access for friendly researchers, closed for anyone who might compete.
value_cards.in_conflict: The researcher with the best question over the one with the biggest budget.
looks_like: Allocating GPU time by research value, not ability to pay
Publishing utilisation data so the community can hold allocators accountable
Rejecting uses that would close rather than open knowledge
value_cards.never_do: Accept a use that benefits one member at the cost of the commons.
value_cards.title: Compute as public infrastructure (edited)

value_cards.because: The atmosphere is a finite buffer. Every year of delay locks in compounding consequences. The technology exists; the bottleneck is manufacturing scale and political inertia.
value_cards.care_about: Moving civilisation off fossil fuels as fast as physically possible — not out of environmentalism but because sustainable energy is simply the correct long-term path.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Treating sustainability as a marketing angle. Optimising vehicle range for luxury buyers over energy density for affordability.
value_cards.in_conflict: Speed of transition over profit margin on any single product.
looks_like: Building the world's largest battery factories before there was demand
Treating the energy problem as a manufacturing problem first
Publishing Tesla's patents openly to accelerate the entire industry
value_cards.never_do: Pretend that incremental improvement is enough.
value_cards.title: Accelerating the energy transition

value_cards.because: Every major AI breakthrough built on decades of public funding and publicly shared research. Privatising the next layer is theft from the commons.
value_cards.care_about: Conducting and sharing research in AI not for competitive advantage but because the knowledge belongs to everyone.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Research published just enough to appear open while keeping the important bits proprietary.
value_cards.in_conflict: The open result over the closed product.
looks_like: Publishing findings before seeking commercial applications
Refusing research that cannot be published
Actively citing and compensating the open-source work we build on
value_cards.never_do: Build on someone's open work without acknowledging it.
value_cards.title: AI research as a gift to humanity

description: A solarpunk neighbourhood where tools, time and skills are shared freely. We grow food, repair what breaks, and look after one another — no money changes hands, only trust.
name: Riverside Commons

value_cards.because: The supermarket is three supply-chain disruptions away from empty shelves. Knowing how to grow is knowing how to survive.
value_cards.care_about: Treating the capacity to grow food as a shared infrastructure — not a lifestyle hobby but a serious community foundation.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Community gardens that only the already-confident use. "Local food" as a premium product rather than a shared right.
value_cards.in_conflict: The person who has never grown anything over the one who knows how.
looks_like: Maintaining at least one communal bed per street
Sharing surplus harvest through the common drop-off rather than letting it rot
Teaching children to grow before they learn to buy
value_cards.never_do: Let knowledge about growing stay locked in one generation.
value_cards.title: Soil and food as commons

value_cards.because: Every skip full of usable things is a failure of connection between neighbours. We have more than enough; we have not yet learned to circulate it.
value_cards.care_about: Making the default assumption that what one household doesn't need, another does — and building the infrastructure for that exchange.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Hoarding under the name of "preparedness". Sharing only the things nobody would want anyway.
value_cards.in_conflict: The collective sufficiency over the individual stockpile.
looks_like: Posting what you're done with before buying new
Borrowing before purchasing for any task that comes up fewer than ten times a year
Fixing the broken thing before the new one arrives
value_cards.never_do: Discard something that a neighbour could use.
value_cards.title: Nothing wasted, everything shared

description: A regenerative growing community restoring soil and pollinators. We swap heirloom seeds, share harvests, and govern the land together through liquid democracy.
name: Earthsong Gardens

value_cards.because: A monoculture requires constant defence. A diverse system defends itself. The garden that thrives with least intervention is the garden that works with nature, not against it.
value_cards.care_about: Designing growing spaces where the cultivated and the wild support each other — not a garden that holds nature at bay but one that invites it in.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Aesthetics that eliminate wildness. Neatness as a value that crowds out biodiversity.
value_cards.in_conflict: The insect over the weed-free path.
looks_like: Leaving areas deliberately unmown and uncultivated
Choosing companion planting over pesticides
Planting for pollinators and birds as deliberately as planting for the table
value_cards.never_do: Remove a plant without first asking what depends on it.
value_cards.title: Wild and cultivated in conversation

value_cards.because: Industrial agriculture has depleted topsoil that took ten thousand years to build in a few decades. We are the generation that either reverses this or doesn't.
value_cards.care_about: Treating the living complexity of healthy soil as the most valuable asset a community can steward — more important than any yield it produces.
value_cards.drift_looks_like: Optimising for visible yield at the cost of invisible soil health. Treating compost as a chore rather than a practice.
value_cards.in_conflict: The soil community over this season's harvest.
looks_like: Testing soil before adding anything to it
Composting all organic waste back into the beds
Leaving roots in the ground to feed the fungal web rather than pulling them
value_cards.never_do: Add a chemical to the soil without understanding what it does to the organisms in it.
value_cards.title: Soil health as the foundation of everything
